qt: to the Commission Juan Ignacio Zoido Álvarez (PPE), Dolors Montserrat (PPE), Javier Zarzalejos (PPE), Alma Ezcurra Almansa (PPE) Subject:

On 30 and 31 July 2026, some 80 000 people entered Ceuta illegally in what – according to recently published police reports – has been deemed a migration instrumentalisation episode. More than a month on, the city continues to be under extraordinary pressure: more than 10 000 immigrants are still on its streets and the strain on reception, migration management and public safety services is intense. Regulation (EU) 2024/1359 establishes a specific framework for addressing exceptional crises and the instrumentalisation of migration. Following a reasoned request from the Member State in question, extraordinary solidarity and support measures and measures to adapt certain asylum procedures can be triggered to bolster capacity to cope with mass arrivals and alleviate the pressure on reception and migration management systems. Given the scale of this state of affairs and the fact that it shows no signs of abating: 1.
Has the Spanish Government asked the Commission to trigger the measures provided for in Regulation (EU) 2024/1359?
If not, does the Commission take the view that the circumstances in Ceuta would justify drawing on that Regulation?
Has the Commission offered the Spanish Government the option to request its activation?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.11.2026) In exceptional situations such as a crisis, including instrumentalisation, or force majeure, a Member State may send a reasoned request to the Commission asking for solidarity support and temporary derogations from certain asylum procedure rules. The Commission has not received a request from the Spanish Government to trigger the measures provided for in Regulation (EU) 2024/13591 following the events in Ceuta, which is a prerogative of the competent authorities of the Member States. The Commission assesses the situation together with the Member State concerned and consults relevant EU agencies and international organisations only upon receiving the reasoned request. In the context of the second Annual Asylum and Migration Management cycle, the Commission concluded that, taking also into account the incident that took place on 30-31 July 2026 leading to large-scale illegal arrivals to the autonomous city of Ceuta, Spain is under migratory pressure2. The Commission has been in close contact with the Spanish authorities regarding the situation in Ceuta since the start of the crisis and has put at the disposal of and provided to Spain all the operational and financial tools available. Nearly EUR 115 million was allocated as emergency funding to Spain in the field of border management, return, reception, including for unaccompanied minors. The EU Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation, the European Border and Coast Guard Agency and the EU Agency for Asylum are also providing additional operational support3.
1 Regulation (EU) 2024/1359 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 May 2024 addressing

situations of crisis and force majeure in the field of migration and asylum and amending Regulation (EU) 2021/1147, PE/19/2024/REV/1, OJ L, 2024/1359, 22.5.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1359/oj. 2 COM(2026) 835 final. 3 https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_26_1799.
